book.title: Wherever You Go, There You Are
book.author: Jon Kabat-Zinn

confidence_note: Secondary summaries only. The invented 80% commute figure and the brain-energy-saving claim were dropped. No named case; concept story from the definition, the automatic-life idea, one thing at a time, and the line on forgetting.
facts: Kabat-Zinn defines mindfulness as paying attention in a particular way: on purpose, in the present moment, and nonjudgmentally.
The book treats meditation as a way to wake up from automatic living.
Much of life runs on automatic and many moments pass without being lived.
The Afterword warns against sleepwalking through life and telling ourselves nice stories.
Practice happens in daily life, in the shower, while eating, while parenting.
The advice is to do one thing at a time.
The book says forgetting to be mindful can teach you a lot more than just being mindful all the time.
scene_details: the moment of noticing you forgot
tension: The book's own definition starts with 'on purpose', which implies that most moments run without anyone choosing them.
opening_idea: Open on the three words 'on purpose' in the definition, and an ordinary shower.

lessons.idea: The moment you notice you drifted counts as the practice, so noticing is the skill.
lessons.anchor: The line that forgetting teaches more than constant mindfulness.

reflect_final: Which one routine this week, a shower, a meal or a commute, will you try doing as the only thing, and what will you notice when you drift?

use_cases.situation: Eating lunch at the desk while answering messages
use_cases.move: Because the book says to do one thing at a time, put the messages away for the first five bites.

use_cases.situation: A colleague says they lost the thread of the call
use_cases.move: Say it is fine to notice drifting; noticing is the point, then return.

use_cases.situation: Helping a child with homework while checking your phone
use_cases.move: Choose one of the two and say it aloud: now it is homework only.

pocket_idea: Noticing that you drifted already counts as practice, so the lapse itself is the lesson.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The definition of mindfulness opens with 'on purpose', which says how many moments are not.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Kabat-Zinn defines mindfulness as attention on purpose, in the present, without judging, and says much of life passes on automatic; his advice is one thing at a time, even in the shower.
